slides.texte_overlay:
small habits that stop
overthinking before it starts

the two minute rule

if a decision takes less than two minutes, make it now. small choices left open pile up in your head and turn into the kind of noise that keeps you awake.

writing it down

when a thought loops, write it on paper exactly as it sounds. seeing it in ink makes it smaller, and your brain stops repeating what it knows is safely stored.

giving your mind something better

an overthinking mind is often just a hungry one, so feed it something calm and interesting: a myth, a planet, a painting. new ideas leave less room for old loops.
slides.texte_sophia:
giving your mind something better

my mind used to loop all evening. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app, a myth or a planet, and giving it something new to chew on quiets the noise.

slides.texte_overlay:
moving your body

when you catch yourself spiralling, walk around the block or stretch for five minutes. moving your body pulls your attention out of your head and back into the room.

setting a worry time

give yourself fifteen minutes a day to worry on purpose. when a worry shows up at another time, tell it to wait, and you'll find most of them never come back.
